 This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

1. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) has been filed by the appellant-insurance company being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 29.04.2015 passed in MVC No.125/2014 by the I Addl. District Judge, MACT,
Raichur (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal', for short) seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

I Addl. District Judge, MACT,
Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel appearing for both parties it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

4. Facts giving rise to the filing of this appeal are that on 11.02.2014 while the deceased was proceeding from Rice Mill on the Hyderabad Shakti Nagar Road, the driver of the Truck bearing registration No.KA-25-A-812 drove it in a rash and negligent manner and applied sudden break and due to which, the deceased fell down from the said Truck and sustained grievous injuries and died in the hospital.
The deceased was Hamali in the said truck and getting salary of Rs.10,000/- per month.
Hence, the claimants preferred a claim petition before the Claims Tribunal seeking compensation.

sentences.text: 2 5. After service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared before the Court and filed written statement denying the contents of claim made by the claimants and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

7. On the basis of material evidence both oral and documentary placed on record and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both the parties, Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.6,65,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a. to the petitioners.
Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioners are before this Court challenging the impugned Judgment and Award.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the claimants and learned counsel for respondent-Insurance Company.
9.
Learned counsel for the appellants has submitted his arguments that the Tribunal has not awarded just and proper compensation.
10. The Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/- per month.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, in respect of the accident of the year 2014, a sum of Rs.7,500/- has to be considered as notional income.
11. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that Tribunal has not awarded compensation towards 'loss of future prospects'.

In view of the law laid down by the Constitutional Bench of the Supreme Court in NATIONAL INSURANCE CO., LTD., VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, to the aforesaid amount, 40% has to be added on account of future prospects as the deceased was aged about 34 years.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE CO., LTD., VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.10,500/-.
Out of which, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th towards personal expenses and therefore, the monthly income comes to Rs.7,875/- (Rs.10,500/- - Rs.2,625/-).

12. As on the date of the accident, the deceased was aged 34 years and the total number of dependents being 4, the Tribunal has committed an error in deducting 1/3rd of his income towards personal expenses.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of SARLA VERMA (SMT)
& OTHERS VS. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION & ANOTHER, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121,

sentences.text: the multiplier applied to the age group of the deceased is 16, which is rightly taken by the tribunal.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.15,12,000/- (Rs.7,875/- x 12 x 16) on account of loss of dependency as against Rs.6,40,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Thus, the petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,12,000/- on account of 'loss of dependency'.
13.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards loss of consortium.

In view of the decision of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. NANU RAM ALIAS CHUHRU RAM & OTHERS reported in 2018 ACJ 2782, a sum of Rs.1,60,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 4) is awarded to the petitioners towards loss of consortium.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- towards funeral expenses, which is on the lower side.
Hence, it would meet the ends of justice if a sum of Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and same is hereby granted.
15. Thus, the petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.17,02,000/- as against Rs.6,65,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.10,37,000/-.
ORDER  (a) The appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.17,02,000/- as against Rs.6,65,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
(c) The petitioners are entitled for  enhanced compensation of Rs.10,37,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till the date of realization of amount.
(d) The Respondent No.2, Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount along with interest, within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
(e) Amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the jurisdictional Tribunal for disbursement of compensation to the petitioners.
(f) The apportionment of the compensation shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
(g) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal shall stand intact.
